pr_title: Set logical_date and data_interval to None for asset-triggered dags and forbid them to be accessed in context/template
pr_body:
## Why
closes: #46192, #46193, #46194, #46196, #46198, #46641

## What
* Set `logical_date` and `data_interval` to None for asset-triggered dags. 
* Not adding `data_interval_start, data_interval_end, prev_data_interval_start_success, prev_data_interval_end_success` if data_interval_start and data_interval_end is None

issue_context.title: AIP-83 2.a. Asset-triggered dag runs will not have a logical date or a data interval
issue_context.body:
### Body

Asset-triggered dag runs will not have a logical date or a data interval

(question 2.a. https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/AIRFLOW/Option+2+clarification+doc+WIP)

### Committer

- [x] I acknowledge that I am a maintainer/committer of the Apache Airflow project.

review_comments: We should be able to do better… this currently takes three queries but we really only need one. I’ll take a look after this PR.

https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/46711#issue-2850147233

created an issue for this. let me think a bit and see whether I can improve it but probably would still be better to do it in another PR
Do we have test cases for non-None values?
Oh I see this test is specific to assets. This is fine.
We should also remove this function from the timetable.
Why do we need to change this?

because if we set `schedule` to something like `AssetOrTimeSchedule(timetable=CronTriggerTimetable("0 1 * * 3", timezone="UTC"), assets=dag1_asset_2)`. the timetable will be periodic even if it's triggered by an asset, which causes the error, as there are no data intervals for such dag runs. Also according to the comment 

```
                # We only publish these metrics for scheduled dag runs and only
                # when ``external_trigger`` is *False* and ``clear_number`` is 0.
```

asset triggered dag runs should not be included

Hmm, OK. We also can’t get rid of `periodic` because e.g. `@once` would have a scheduled run but that shouldn’t be counted as periodic. (OR… maybe we can choose to change the behaviour in those cases? That’s a different discussion I guess.)
